experiment.title: Frozen first-norm semantics, Hilbert rank caps, and source-span diagnostic
experiment.objective: Independently validate the degree-preserving norm identity and exact finite-registry TT rank caps on frozen toy instances, measure the fixed source-tensor span and honest enumeration costs, and produce a reviewed implementation contract for the subsequent coefficient-space advice construction. This run is a semantic diagnostic, not an asymptotic benchmark.
controls: rank-one separable tensor with exact ranks (1,1,1,1)
synthetic quadratic norm tensor whose rank grows above one
projective rescaling of every registered input and target
direct affine group sum used only for projective and zero-set replay
independent_variables: tensor kind g_Q, h_Q, or h_Q^e

primary: mismatch count between g_Q*conjugate(g_Q) and e_X^2+trace*e_X*e_Y+norm*e_Y^2
mismatch count between generator and independent verifier values
exact unfolding ranks of g_Q over F_p2
exact unfolding ranks of h_Q and diagnostic powers over F_p
Hilbert cap and rank-to-cap ratio for every cut
independent source-span residual count and target-family span dimension
zero-set mismatch count against independent affine group addition
secondary: RCB gate and base-field operation counts
logical field words read and written
SHA-256 digest and deterministic samples of each tensor
raw product bond dimensions distinguished from exact ranks
source advice, preprocessing, and online specialization accounting kept in separate ledgers

stopping_rules: Stop and preserve the run if any primary semantic mismatch occurs.
Stop before allocating any predicted object above 2 GB.
Stop before dense materialization of the 9216 by 13824 coefficient flattening or any larger power flattening.
Stop and require a versioned specification repair if the frozen manifest or circuit hash changes.
Do not stop merely because a toy middle rank equals B^2; this is permitted by the Hilbert bound for B at most 96.
invalidation_rules: Any primary curve, registry, target, extension basis, mode order, tree, or gate is selected after rank observation.
Any primary registry contains duplicate affine points or duplicate identifiers.
The generator and verifier import the same RCB, norm, rank, or tuple-order implementation.
Affine addition is used to assign nonzero tensor values or ranks.
Literal polynomial Frobenius degree pD is conflated with coefficient conjugation on F_p inputs.
Rank over F_p2 is reported for an F_p-valued matrix without independently checking base-field rank equality.
Full enumeration, failed attempts, memory, traffic, exact normalization, or certificate replay is omitted from accounting.
A toy rank trend or fixed-power result is fitted as an asymptotic exponent.
experiment.success_criterion: All frozen primary and control cases replay with zero semantic, source-span, zero-set, and projective-rescaling mismatches; all exact h_Q ranks satisfy their ambient-capped Hilbert bounds; every registered mutation is detected; and the run emits complete operation, memory, traffic, and provenance ledgers. This supports only the restricted first-norm theorem and authorizes a separate coefficient-space advice-construction experiment.
experiment.falsification_criterion: Any valid independently reproduced mismatch or rank-bound violation rejects the corresponding theorem implementation. Failure to build compact source advice narrows the constructive compiler hypothesis but does not falsify the Hilbert upper bound. Toy ambient saturation and resource refusal for a prohibited dense matrix are not falsification.
